= Yubnub ecosystem research — GitHub, archive.org, Blue Squirrel (2026-10-13) =

*Follow-up to [`../yubnub-deep-dive.md`](../yubnub-deep-dive.md): where does
Yubnub live on in code, what replaced it, and what do the archives hold?
Method: `gh search repos` / `gh repo view` / GitHub API (authenticated),
archive.org AdvancedSearch + Metadata + Wayback CDX APIs, vendor site fetch.
All counts are as observed 2026-10-13.*

---

== 1. GitHub — the original and its clients ==

| Repo | ★ | Last push | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [JonathanAquino/yubnub](https://github.com/JonathanAquino/yubnub) | 57 | 2026-10-01 | **The original author's repo** — "A social command line for the web". GitHub now classes it as PHP (the production codebase outgrew the 2005 Rails Day entry). This is the link to cite. |
| [jcnetdev/yubnub](https://github.com/jcnetdev/yubnub) | 31 | ~2021 | The Rails 2.1 refactor ("Source Code (v3)" era). Historically important, effectively frozen. |
| [hrichardlee/YubNubEx](https://github.com/hrichardlee/YubNubEx) | 2 | 2021 | Chrome extension — the one linked from yubnub.org's *Installing* page. Local overrides + multi-tab searches. |
| [lilyball/yubnubsearch](https://github.com/lilyball/yubnubsearch) | 3 | 2019 | SIMBL plugin turning Safari's search field into a Yubnub field (the Kevin Ballard plugin the docs mention). |
| [titosemi/yubnub](https://github.com/titosemi/yubnub) | 2 | 2014 | Bash console client (`curl`/`wget` against `parser/parse`, pluggable openers incl. w3m). |
| jontsao/NoStone · Natook/Yubnub-widget | 1 | 2014 | Chrome extension / widget experiments. |

Noise to ignore when searching: at least four unrelated repos named
`YubNub`/`Yubnub` (a Discord music bot, SWAPI iOS app, streaming site,
school project) — "yub nub" is also the Ewok celebration song from
*Return of the Jedi*, which pollutes every search (see §3).

== 2. GitHub — clones, replacements, and the successor lineage ==

**Direct clones / self-hosted replacements** (the "run your own Yubnub" idea):

| Repo | ★ | Last push | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [dohliam/yub](https://github.com/dohliam/yub) | 14 | 2022 | **yub.js** — the closest living relative. Fully client-side, hosted at dohliam.github.io/yub. `js/engines.js` counted for this research: **138 engines** (`g`, `gim`, `sp`, `ix`, `gmail`, `drive`, `wbm`…). Explicitly born from a bookmark file of ex-Yubnub commands. |
| [cldwalker/queriac](https://github.com/cldwalker/queriac) | 7 | 2008 | "Picking up where Yubnub left off" — the earliest successor attempt, Ruby. |
| [pesterhazy/shub](https://github.com/pesterhazy/shub) | 3 | 2023 | "Search Engine Hub, like yubnub" — minimal redirect service for Chrome/Opera. |
| [arne-schroppe/webcmd](https://github.com/arne-schroppe/webcmd) | 2 | 2017 | Locally hosted replacement; `~/.webcmd.json`, browser engine at `localhost:8000/?q=%s`. |
| [profmaad/webcli](https://github.com/profmaad/webcli) | 2 | archived | "A yubnub-style search provider, running locally." |
| [sabberworm/YoubNub](https://github.com/sabberworm/YoubNub) | 1 | 2015 | JavaScript "YubNub clone". |
| [szaboat/nodenub](https://github.com/szaboat/nodenub) | 1 | 2015 | "Yubnub like server written in node.js." |
| [asymmetric/RubNub](https://github.com/asymmetric/RubNub) | 0 | archived | Ruby clone (not the Firefox RubNub extension of the same name). |

**The idea, productised elsewhere:**

- **Bunnylol / bunny1 lineage** — Facebook's internal "smart bookmarks"
  (`gh` → GitHub, etc.), open-sourced as
  [facebook/bunnylol.rs](https://github.com/facebook/bunnylol.rs)
  (149 ★, Rust, pushed 2026-10-10 — actively maintained), plus
  rithik/bunnylol (66 ★), taneliang/neh (34 ★), markusdosch/gopherlol (Go),
  mic47/platypuslol (Rust). Same insight as Yubnub — one keyword router for
  the whole web — but private/team-scoped instead of a public commons.
- **golinks** — [prologic/golinks](https://github.com/prologic/golinks)
  (16 ★) and dhutty/golinks (3 ★): "smart bookmarks, commands and aliases
  by pointing your browser's default search engine at a running instance.
  Similar to bunny1, yubnub." This is the entry **awesome-selfhosted**
  carries — which explains §3's archive noise.
- **DuckDuckGo !bangs** — the mainstream successor UX (suffix `!g`/`!w`
  instead of Yubnub's prefix). Ecosystem repos: zmwangx/ddg-bangs
  (scraper/registry), ewasion/everybody-do-the-bang (kept-current list),
  jameshealyio/bang-bookmarks (124 ★, Firefox Keymarks), dkarter/Bang
  (Alfred). Bangs won on distribution; Yubnub's `${switches}` + `{pipes}`
  remain strictly more expressive.
- **AlternativeTo** lists only Ubiquity (Mozilla's natural-language
  commander, discontinued) and Shortmarks for Yubnub — both effectively
  historical. LibHunt's yub.js alternatives page corroborates the
  bunnylol/bangs neighbourhood.

**Verdict:** no maintained public Yubnub clone exists. The maintained code
is (a) Aquino's own repo, (b) yub.js for client-side use, (c) bunnylol.rs
for team use. That's precisely the gap this repo's offline
[`yubnub.html`](../yubnub.html) fills.

== 3. archive.org — crawlers, and a homonym trap ==

- Text search `yubnub` → **46 hits, almost all noise**: awesome-selfhosted
  GitHub mirrors (they mention golinks, above) and Ewok material.
- ⚠️ Identifier [`YubNub`](https://archive.org/details/YubNub) is **not
  software** — it's the "Ewok Celebration (Yub Nub)" MP3 from the 1983
  *Return of the Jedi* theatrical cut. Do not cite it as a Yubnub archive.
- The real software-history item:
  [`wiki-editthisinfo_yubnub`](https://archive.org/details/wiki-editthisinfo_yubnub)
  — a **WikiTeam dump (2014-01-17)** of the Yubnub wiki
  (`editthis.info/yubnub`, the wiki the homepage links to): MediaWiki XML
  dump + full history, 7z, uploaded 2014-07-21. The only preserved copy of
  the community command documentation wiki.
- **Wayback CDX**: `yubnub.org` is captured from **2005-06-20** (days after
  the Rails Day launch) continuously to the present — the command corpus
  (`kernel/ls` pages) is replayable there even though the live corpus is
  not bulk-downloadable.
- **Crawler software in the Tucows Software Library** (donated by Tucows
  "for long term preservation"): `tucows_336323_Grab-A-Site` (2003),
  `tucows_205130_WebWhacker` (2000), `tucows_193819_WebWhacker` (2002),
  `WEBWHK_zip_20` (WebWhacker v2.0 Beta, 1996), `DGRAB3_ZIP`
  (Grab a Site v3, 1996), plus manuals (`manualzilla` WebWhacker /
  Grab-a-Site). These are the period-correct tools for crawling a site
  like yubnub.org wholesale — the 1996–2003 ancestors of `wget --mirror`.

== 4. Blue Squirrel — not abandonware (yet) ==

Blue Squirrel (founded 1995, Utah — bluesquirrel.com) matters here twice
over:

1. **Conceptual ancestor.** Their first product was **SQURL — "Search and
   Query URLs"** — replaced by **WebSeeker**, a meta-search/query-URL tool
   that, in their words, was "searching the entire web before Google was
   born". SQURL→WebSeeker is the commercial 1995 expression of the same
   idea Yubnub socialised in 2005: named, parameterised query URLs.
   Sibling "Seeker" products: TechSeeker, LegalSeeker.
2. **The crawlers.** **WebWhacker** ("the first offline browser" — copy a
   whole site to hard drive/CD and browse it as if online) and
   **Grab-a-Site** (multi-threaded site mirroring with file-type filters)
   are exactly the "archive.org crawlers" class of tool. ForeFront
   (NASDAQ: FFGI) acquired Blue Squirrel in 1997 as its Internet Content
   Management Division, keeping the product names.

**Abandonware status: NO.** Verified 2026-10-13: bluesquirrel.com is live
and selling (ClickBook for Windows/Mac — Mac at version 5; 30-day
money-back guarantee page up). WebWhacker's latest build is **5.0.0.18
(2020-10-24)**, $49.95 shareware per the Software Informer listing.
What *is* legitimately preserved on archive.org:

- [`blue-squirrel-catalog-vol-1`](https://archive.org/details/blue-squirrel-catalog-vol-1)
  — the 1998-05-15 retail CD (62.5 MB, "imaged from an original disc with
  no errors"): WebSeeker, TechSeeker, LegalSeeker, WebWhacker,
  Grab-a-Site, GrabNet, LinkSync, ClickBook, Internet Automation System.
- The Tucows items in §3 (Tucows-donated preservation copies).

So: cite and link these, don't redistribute the binaries in this repo —
the vendor is alive, and the archive.org copies already do the
preservation job properly.

== 5. What this changed in the app ==

- Registry: imported 4 commands from the yub.js audit with modernised
  hosts — `sp` (Startpage), `gmails` (Gmail search), `gdrive`
  (Drive search), `ud` (Urban Dictionary) — flagged **new**.
- Link crawl tab: added JonathanAquino/yubnub (primary source),
  dohliam/yub, facebook/bunnylol.rs, the Blue Squirrel catalog CD, and
  the WikiTeam Yubnub dump; corrected the Source Code credit (was
  jcnetdev only).
- [`yubnub-deep-dive.md`](../yubnub-deep-dive.md) §1/§6 source lines
  updated to match.
